children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine whether you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me: **How many children are you enquiring about, and what are their names?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Thanks for helping me with this. I'm asking about my one child - my son Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So I'm assessing eligibility for your son, Alex.

Let me start by asking: **How old is Alex?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. That's helpful to know.

Next, **do you currently live with Alex in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, that's the thing - Alex lives with me, but we don't actually live in the UK at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I see. That's an important detail.

**Which country do you and Alex currently live in?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: We're living abroad right now - we moved overseas a while back.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. I can see that you're living abroad, which does affect Child Benefit eligibility.

To help determine if you might still be eligible, I need to know a bit more: **Are you a UK citizen, or do you have any specific immigration status such as settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, or are you a Crown servant?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm just a regular UK citizen - nothing special like Crown servant status or anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

Since you're a UK citizen living abroad with Alex, I need to check one more important detail: **Did you move abroad temporarily, or is this a permanent move? In other words, do you intend to return to the UK at some point, or have you permanently relocated?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: We've relocated - it's not just a temporary thing. We're settled here now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I appreciate you clarifying that. Since you've permanently relocated abroad and are settled there, I have enough information to assess your eligibility.

Based on the Child Benefit rules, eligibility is normally dependent on living in the UK. While there are some exceptions for people who move to certain countries or who are Crown servants, the guidance indicates that you would need to check the specific rules about living abroad.

However, since you've indicated you're a regular UK citizen (not a Crown servant) who has permanently relocated abroad, this would typically fall outside the standard eligibility criteria for Child Benefit.

Let me confirm one final detail to be thorough: **Are you currently receiving any UK state benefits, or do you have any other ties to the UK that might be relevant - such as paying UK taxes or National Insurance contributions?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not receiving any UK benefits at the moment, and I don't have those kinds of ties to the UK anymore.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for confirming that. I now have sufficient information to provide you with my assessment.

**Summary:**

I'm afraid you are **not eligible for Child Benefit** for Alex at this time.

**Why:** While Alex meets the age requirement (being 6 years old, under 16) and you are clearly responsible for him as his parent, Child Benefit eligibility requires that you live in the UK. Since you have permanently relocated abroad and are now settled there with no ongoing ties to the UK, you fall outside the standard eligibility criteria.

Although there are some exceptions for people who live in certain countries or who have specific statuses (like Crown servants), these don't apply to your situation as a regular UK citizen living abroad.

**Next steps:** If you believe your circumstances might qualify for any exceptions, or if your situation changes in the future (such as if you return to the UK), you may wish to contact the Child Benefit Office directly for further guidance.
